subject: Polity
description: House of People: composition, term, qualifications, sessions

questions.stem: The MAXIMUM strength of the LOK SABHA, as per the Constitution, is:
questions.explanation: Article 81 — Maximum LS strength = 552: 530 from STATES + 20 from UTs + 2 ANGLO-INDIAN nominees (originally; REMOVED by 104th Amendment, 2019). NOW = 543 actual elected members (530 from states + 13 from UTs). India is currently in 18th Lok Sabha (June 2024). Term = 5 years (Article 83) unless dissolved sooner; can be extended by 1 year during emergency.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The MINIMUM AGE to contest as a Lok Sabha candidate is:
questions.explanation: Article 84(b) — minimum age for LS candidate = 25 years. Other minimums: RAJYA SABHA candidate = 30 years; PRESIDENT + Vice President = 35; Governor = 35. Voter (electorate) age = 18 (lowered from 21 by 61st Amendment, 1989). LS member must also: be Indian citizen, registered voter in any constituency, not hold office of profit (Article 102 — disqualifications). 'Anti-defection' (10th Schedule) — defection grounds for disqualification.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The QUORUM (minimum members for LS sitting) is what fraction of total membership?
questions.explanation: Article 100(3) — Quorum for either House = 1/10 of total membership (Speaker / Chairman included). LS quorum = 543/10 ≈ 55. RS quorum = 245/10 ≈ 25. If quorum not met during a sitting, Speaker / Chairman ADJOURNS the House. The threshold is intentionally low — to allow business when many MPs are away. 1/10 was chosen by Constituent Assembly (Ambedkar's recommendation).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Lok Sabha can be DISSOLVED by:

options.option_text: Speaker of the Lok Sabha by motion
President on PM's advice (or expiry of 5 yrs)
Vote of all state legislative assemblies

questions.explanation: Article 85 — President SUMMONS, prorogues, dissolves Parliament. PRESIDENT dissolves LS — typically on PRIME MINISTER's advice. Or LS dissolves automatically at end of its 5-year term. AFTER dissolution → general elections must be held (within 6 months — though practically faster). Speaker continues until day before new LS first sitting. Note: Rajya Sabha is PERMANENT — never dissolved (1/3 retire every 2 years). Distractor 1 — Speaker can't dissolve (he/she only presides). Distractor 3 — SC can't dissolve.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Lok Sabha is also called the:

options.option_text: Council of States, in upper house terms
Vidhan Sabha, in state legislature only

questions.explanation: Article 79 — Parliament = President + Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha. LOK SABHA = 'HOUSE OF THE PEOPLE' (lower house, directly elected, popular house). RAJYA SABHA = 'COUNCIL OF STATES' (upper house, indirectly elected by state MLAs + nominated). State versions: VIDHAN SABHA (Legislative Assembly) + VIDHAN PARISHAD (Legislative Council; only 6 states have it). 'Lok Sabha' name from Hindi 'lok' (people) + 'sabha' (assembly).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The MAXIMUM GAP between two sessions of the Lok Sabha cannot exceed:
questions.explanation: Article 85 — Parliament must meet at least TWICE A YEAR. Maximum gap between two SESSIONS = 6 MONTHS (i.e., between last sitting of one session + first sitting of next). Three SESSIONS by convention each year: BUDGET (Jan-Apr); MONSOON (Jul-Sep); WINTER (Nov-Dec). PROROGATION = ending a session (President's order). DISSOLUTION = ending the LS itself. ADJOURNMENT = pausing within a session (Speaker can do).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: FIRST HOUR of every working day in the Lok Sabha is called:

options.option_text: Zero Hour, named after British use

questions.explanation: QUESTION HOUR (11 AM-12 PM) — first hour of every parliamentary working day. MPs ask QUESTIONS to ministers; ministers answer + are held accountable. Three types: STARRED (oral, requires oral answer + supplementary); UNSTARRED (written answer, no supplementary); SHORT NOTICE (urgent matters, up to 10 days notice). ZERO HOUR (12 noon-1 PM) — Indian innovation (1962); MPs raise urgent matters without prior notice. Most TV-attention-grabbing time. Both 'hours' have been observed less in recent times due to disruptions.
